meta.title: Florida and Miami grant and assistance programs for small businesses and nonprofits
meta.rules: Every entry was opened on its official page on 2026-10-25 and its URL checked live (curl with a browser User-Agent, following redirects; WebFetch where the site bot-checks curl). Amounts and deadlines are quoted as stated; null means the official page did not state it. Nothing invented. Status: open = accepting now; rolling = accepted until funds run out; closed = not accepting now; unclear = page gives no current dates.
meta.rechecked: All official_url links re-checked 2026-10-25 ~10:35 AM ET: 200 OK except miami.gov and miamidda.com pages (403 to scripted curl, loaded fine in a browser fetch) and floridahumanities.org, miamifoundation.org, elevatesmall.biz (bot-check 202, page content confirmed by browser fetch).

programs.name: Mom and Pop Small Business Grant Program
programs.administrator: Miami-Dade County Board of County Commissioners (district offices); administered with Neighbors and Neighbors Association, Inc. (NANA)
programs.eligibility_detail: For-profit small business physically located in the specific county commission district; not part of a national chain; physical address required (home-based businesses can apply); W-9, Local Business Tax certificate and licenses required. Each district sets extra criteria.
programs.amount: Varies by district: up to $5,000 (e.g. Districts 6 and 9, 2026); up to $1,500 (District 5, 2026)
programs.deadline: closed - next cycle TBD
programs.notes: County page lists all 13 districts as 'No longer accepting applications.' The latest 2026 cycle was District 9 (hand-delivered applications Oct 5-9, 2026). Runs annually per district; good 'come back next year' item.
programs.source_quote: District 1 ... District 13: 'No longer accepting applications.' | D9 release: 'receive up to $5,000 in grant funding ... Completed applications must be hand-delivered ... from Oct. 5 through Oct. 9 by 4 p.m.' | D5 release: 'grants of up to $1,500'

programs.name: Commercial Facade Treatment Program
programs.administrator: City of Miami Department of Housing & Community Development, delivered through district Community Based Organizations (CBOs)
programs.eligibility_detail: Operating for-profit business with a valid occupational license and certificate of use for the location, in a census tract with 51%+ low-income residents that is primarily residential; work must be exterior and visible from a commercial corridor. Apply via the CBO for your commission district. Match of 5-15% required.
programs.amount: Up to 85% of facade costs on a maximum of $10,000 of work (max $8,500 covered)
programs.deadline: rolling - subject to funding availability
programs.notes: Eligible work: pressure cleaning/painting, awnings, doors, signs, security shutters. Page warns demand often exceeds funding. CAMACOL runs it for Districts 3 and 4 (camacol.org/facade, not separately verified).
programs.source_quote: 'The City provides up to 85% of facade enhancement costs for a maximum of $10,000 worth of work. That means a maximum of $8,500 of you costs could be covered' ... 'This program operates based on funding availability.'

programs.name: Commercial Code Compliance Program
programs.administrator: City of Miami Department of Housing & Community Development (via CBOs)
programs.eligibility_detail: Commercial property owners / for-profit businesses with a Code Enforcement violation, same low-income census-tract rules as the facade program.
programs.amount: Up to 85% of code compliance costs on a maximum of $15,000 of work (max $12,750 covered)
programs.deadline: closed - next cycle TBD
programs.notes: Same page as the facade program; this one currently has no funding.
programs.source_quote: 'The City provides up to 85% of the your code compliance costs for a maximum of $15,000 worth of work ... There is no funding in this program at this time.'

programs.name: District 4 Facade Improvement Grant
programs.administrator: City of Miami District 4 Commissioner's office, in partnership with Sunshine for All
programs.eligibility_detail: Any business in the low-income areas of City of Miami District 4 (landlord approval needed if not the owner). 10% match.
programs.deadline: rolling - first-come, first-served while funds last
programs.notes: Page says 'The project launches May 5th and funds are limited' but does not state the year or whether funds remain. Uses: exterior paint/pressure cleaning, signage, awnings, windows/doors. Treat as 'check with office'.
programs.source_quote: 'Businesses ... can receive grants of up to $10,000 with a 10% match.' 'The project launches May 5th and funds are limited. Applicants will be considered on a first-come, first-serve basis.'

programs.name: Property Improvement Grant Program
programs.administrator: Miami Downtown Development Authority (Miami DDA); administered by Downtown Miami Partnership
programs.eligibility_detail: Downtown Miami (DDA district) property owners/businesses doing pre-approved exterior improvements; aimed at retail and restaurants. Independent committee review.
programs.amount: Up to 50% of actual cost of pre-approved exterior improvements, not to exceed $50,000
programs.deadline: annual cycle - check page (no deadline stated)
programs.notes: No application deadline shown on the page; guidelines and application PDFs are linked there.
programs.source_quote: 'The Program provides grants for up to 50% of the actual cost of pre-approved qualifying exterior property improvements, not to exceed $50.000.'

programs.name: Miami DDA Business Incentive Grants
programs.administrator: Miami Downtown Development Authority
programs.eligibility_detail: Businesses relocating to or expanding in Downtown Miami: ground-floor retail, ground-floor food & beverage, tech start-ups, mid-sized businesses.
programs.deadline: annual cycle - check page (no deadline stated)
programs.notes: Amounts are in a linked one-pager PDF, not verified.
programs.source_quote: 'offering grants to businesses relocating or expanding within its vibrant districts. Grants are available for ground-floor retail, ground-floor food & beverage establishments, tech start-ups and mid-sized businesses.'

programs.name: SEOPW CRA Small Business Grant Program
programs.administrator: Southeast Overtown/Park West Community Redevelopment Agency (City of Miami)
programs.eligibility_detail: Small businesses operating within the SEOPW (Overtown/Park West) redevelopment area.
programs.deadline: rolling - first-come, first-served
programs.notes: Apply by email or hand-deliver to the Overtown Business Resource Center (1490 NW 3rd Ave, Suite 106) or SEOPW CRA office (819 NW 2nd Ave, 3rd Floor), Tue-Thu 10am-4pm. Award size not stated on the official page (press reports of ~$5,000 not verified).
programs.source_quote: 'offers direct funding to eligible local businesses to help offset operational costs, invest in infrastructure ... Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis'

programs.name: SEOPW CRA Public Art Activation and Community Beautification Grant Program
programs.administrator: Southeast Overtown/Park West Community Redevelopment Agency
programs.eligibility_detail: Projects within SEOPW CRA boundaries creating permanent or semi-permanent public art / place-based improvements (artists, organizations, property owners).
programs.deadline: Grant period October 2026 - February 2027, subject to funding availability
programs.notes: Online application (fillable PDF upload) on the page. Eligibility details are in the downloadable guidelines (not reviewed).
programs.source_quote: 'Grant Period: October 2026 - February 2027, subject to funding availability.'

programs.name: Omni CRA Business Assistance Microgrant
programs.administrator: Omni Community Redevelopment Agency (City of Miami)
programs.eligibility_detail: Business or property owners inside Omni CRA district boundaries: new business openings, code violations, ADA access, business interruption/disaster recovery, hiring/training, building improvements. Private match expected.
programs.deadline: rolling - as funding permits
programs.notes: The 'Download the Business Assistance Program Application' link on the official page points to a 2024 guidelines PDF; confirm it is still current with the CRA (305-679-6868, OmniCRA@miamigov.com).
programs.source_quote: 'The Microgrant Program has a project cap of $35,000.' ... 'Grantees are selected on a rolling basis at the discretion of the executive staff as funding permits.'

programs.name: Community Engagement & Outreach Grants (CEOG 2026-08/09)
programs.administrator: The Children's Trust (Miami-Dade)
programs.eligibility_detail: Organizations with existing direct-service programs or outreach events for Miami-Dade children and families; not eligible if currently receiving other Children's Trust funding (except Small CBO capacity building and Innovation Fund). One award per org per fiscal year.
programs.amount: Typical award under $20,000 (Direct Service Program Enhancement); under $10,000 (Outreach)
programs.deadline: closed - applications were due July 30, 2026; next cycle TBD
programs.notes: Annual-looking cycle (released June, due July, contracts start Oct 1). Good fit for small community groups.
programs.source_quote: 'Application Deadline: July 30, 2026 by 5:00 PM' ... 'The typical grant award is expected to be less than $20,000.00.' ... 'less than $10,000.00.'

programs.name: Public Humanities Program Grants
programs.administrator: Florida Humanities
programs.eligibility_detail: Florida-based nonprofits, state/local governments, federally recognized tribes; need SAM.gov UEI and FEIN. Not individuals, for-profits, or fiscally sponsored projects. Priority for orgs with budgets under $500,000 and first-time applicants.
programs.deadline: closed - Fall 2026 final applications were due Aug 5, 2026; next cycle TBD (two cycles a year: spring and fall)
programs.notes: Requires a Letter of Interest first. Fetched via WebFetch (curl got a bot-check 202).
programs.source_quote: 'Funding Amount: Up to $10,000' ... 'Deadlines Fall 2026 ... Final Applications Due August 5, 2026 @ 12 PM EST'

programs.name: General Program Support (GPS)
programs.administrator: Florida Department of State, Division of Arts and Culture
programs.eligibility_detail: Public entities or Florida nonprofit, tax-exempt corporations doing arts/cultural programming (operating support).
programs.deadline: closed - FY2027-28 window closed July 10, 2026; next deadline TBD
programs.notes: All Division grants are pending legislative appropriation.
programs.source_quote: 'Applications for Fiscal Year 2027-2028 are CLOSED / Next Deadline: TBD' | dosgrants.com: 'designed to fund up to $150,000 for the general program activities of an organization' (application period 6/1/2026 - 7/10/2026)

programs.name: Specific Cultural Project (SCP) grants
programs.administrator: Florida Department of State, Division of Arts and Culture
programs.eligibility_detail: Public entities, Florida nonprofit tax-exempt organizations, and (Artist Project category) individual professional artists who are Florida residents 18+.
programs.deadline: closed - FY2027-28 window closed July 10, 2026; next deadline TBD
programs.notes: The old SCP program URL under /grant-programs/ returned 404; using the Division's application page + official guidelines PDF.
programs.source_quote: '2027-2028 Fiscal Year application window is CLOSED for: General Program Support, Specific Cultural Projects, Cultural Facilities' | Guidelines: 'provide funding up to $25,000 for a specific artistic/cultural project'

programs.name: Historic Preservation Small Matching Grants
programs.administrator: Florida Department of State, Division of Historical Resources
programs.eligibility_detail: Local, regional and statewide historic preservation efforts (nonprofits and governments); not operating support.
programs.deadline: closed - FY2028 cycle ran June 1 - July 10, 2026; next cycle TBD
programs.notes: Same page covers Special Category and Abandoned African-American Cemeteries grants (same dates). Amounts are in guidelines (not verified).
programs.source_quote: 'will open the FY2028 application cycles for Small Matching, Special Category, and Abandoned African-American Cemetery grants on June 1, 2026, and close them at 5:00 p.m. (Eastern) on July 10, 2026.'

programs.name: Knight Cities Challenge (2026)
programs.administrator: John S. and James L. Knight Foundation
programs.eligibility_detail: Project ideas serving one of 26 Knight communities (Miami is one) on local information, economic opportunity, or arts/culture connection; projects completed within one year.
programs.deadline: closed - applications were open April 1-30, 2026; second cohort timing TBD
programs.notes: $10 million over two cohorts across three years; up to $5 million in the first round. Strong pitch example of a big local challenge grant.
programs.source_quote: 'KCC will support projects in 26 communities across the country, with grants of up to $200,000.' 'Applications are now open from April 1-30.'

programs.name: Community Grants Program
programs.administrator: The Miami Foundation
programs.eligibility_detail: Active 501(c)(3) public charities (or fiscally sponsored projects), government entities, nonprofit-equivalent religious orgs; work must directly serve Miami-Dade residents. Two years of general operating support.
programs.deadline: closed - reopens in 2027
programs.notes: Award size depends on operating budget (ranges in guidelines, not verified). $7 million invested over two years in the 2025-27 cycle. Fetched via WebFetch (curl got 202 bot-check).
programs.source_quote: 'The 2025-27 Community Grants application cycle has closed.' 'Community Grants will open applications in 2027.'

programs.name: Press Forward South Florida Open Call (Newsroom Strength + Collaboration)
programs.administrator: Press Forward South Florida (housed at The Miami Foundation)
programs.eligibility_detail: South Florida local news organizations.
programs.amount: $20,000 to $100,000 over two years (collaboration category); $20,000 stipend (newsroom strength)
programs.deadline: closed - deadline was July 24, 2026
programs.notes: Niche (news orgs only).
programs.source_quote: 'The deadline for this grant has passed.' 'The deadline to apply for these grants is July 24, 2026.' 'grants between $20,000 and $100,000 over two years.'

programs.name: Incumbent Worker Training (IWT) Grant
programs.administrator: CareerSource Florida
programs.eligibility_detail: For-profit Florida companies (or hospitals) operating at least 1 year, training existing full-time W-2 employees (6+ months tenure). Apply at least 45 business days before training starts. Reimburses up to 50% of training costs (up to 75% for 25 or fewer employees, rural, distressed, brownfield or HUBZone).
programs.amount: Up to $100,000 per grant per company (FY2026-27 pool: $3 million)
programs.deadline: rolling - FY July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 while funds last
programs.notes: One of the few clearly OPEN, for-profit-friendly state grants today. Reimbursement grant (you pay first).
programs.source_quote: Guidelines (July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027): 'Fiscal Year 2026-2027 (July 1 - June 30) $3 Million. The maximum amount is $100,000 per grant per company.' 'Applications must be submitted at least 45 business days prior to the desired start date.'

programs.name: Quick Response Training (QRT) Grant
programs.administrator: CareerSource Florida
programs.eligibility_detail: Businesses in Florida's qualified targeted industries creating new jobs and needing customized training; priority to first-time applicants.
programs.deadline: rolling - until funds are no longer available
programs.notes: Page still cites the 2025/2026 allocation; check current-year funding before promising. Targeted-industry list applies, so many Main Street businesses won't qualify.
programs.source_quote: '$7.5 million has been allocated for the Quick Response Training program in 2025/2026. Priority will be given to businesses applying for the first time. A notification will be posted here when funds are no longer available.'

programs.name: Florida Small Business Emergency Bridge Loan (Hurricane Isaias)
programs.administrator: FloridaCommerce
programs.eligibility_detail: Small businesses with economic injury or physical damage from Hurricane Isaias (Panhandle; canvassing covered Escambia, Okaloosa, Santa Rosa and Walton counties). Not applicable to Miami-Dade.
programs.deadline: 2026-11-25 (or until funds are exhausted)
programs.notes: Short-term, interest-free loan, not a grant. Activated per disaster. Loan maximums were not stated on the official pages fetched.
programs.source_quote: Governor's release (Oct 2026): 'provides short-term, no-interest loans to small businesses that experienced economic injury or physical damage due to Hurricane Isaias. Interested applicants can apply now through November 25, 2026, or until all available funds are exhausted'

programs.name: Target Sector Trade Show Grants
programs.administrator: SelectFlorida (Florida's trade and export partner)
programs.eligibility_detail: Florida-registered company in business 2+ years in Florida, with a commercial office/warehouse/factory (no home-based), 3-500 full-time employees, $250,000+ annual sales, Florida-made product or Florida-based service; for trade shows on SelectFlorida's calendar.
programs.deadline: rolling - event-specific (contact grant representative)
programs.notes: Reimbursement grant for exhibiting at international trade shows. The cost-share amount sits in a page tab that was not captured; amount left null.
programs.source_quote: 'SelectFlorida provides event-specific grants on a reimbursable basis to eligible manufacturers and select professional services providers in target sectors.'

programs.name: Florida SBDC at FIU (no-cost business consulting)
programs.administrator: Florida SBDC Network / FIU College of Business
programs.eligibility_detail: Businesses in Miami-Dade or Monroe with 3+ employees, or launching a scalable venture. Does not give loans or grants; helps find and package them.
programs.deadline: rolling
programs.notes: Free help partner to name in the pitch.
programs.source_quote: 'offer confidential, no-cost consulting ... If you own a business with 3 or more employees, or are launching a scalable venture' ... 'Florida SBDC centers do not provide loans nor investment capital'

programs.name: Florida APEX Accelerator at FIU (government contracting help)
programs.administrator: Florida APEX Accelerator network (FIU center)
programs.eligibility_detail: Florida businesses pursuing federal, state and local government contracts; FIU center serves Miami-Dade and Monroe.
programs.deadline: rolling
programs.notes: Contacts listed on official page: Luis Batista (lubatist@fiu.edu), Nari Tomlinson (ntomlins@fiu.edu), 305-779-9230. Not contacted.
programs.source_quote: 'offers government contracting consulting and training at no cost to ready businesses.' | Locations: 'Florida APEX Accelerator at FIU ... Serving the following counties: Miami-Dade, Monroe'

programs.name: Miami-Dade Small Business Enterprise (SBE) Certification
programs.administrator: Miami-Dade County Strategic Procurement Department, Small Business Development (SBD)
programs.eligibility_detail: Categories SBE-Goods & Services, SBE-Construction, SBE-A&E; e.g. average gross receipts over past 3 years not over $8 million (G&S/Construction). Valid 3 years.
programs.deadline: rolling
programs.notes: Not money, but unlocks SBE set-aside county contracts; required for SBE set-aside county contracts.
programs.source_quote: 'Certification for a SBE firm is valid for a three-year period.' 'Average gross receipts over the past 3 years must not exceed $8 million'

programs.name: MDEAT Small Business Capitalization Grant (Business Empowerment Blueprint)
programs.administrator: Miami-Dade Economic Advocacy Trust (MDEAT)
programs.eligibility_detail: Miami-Dade for-profits (and nonprofits, separate criteria) in existence 3+ years on Sunbiz, average revenue $24,000-$750,000 over last 3 years, attend a grant-cycle workshop; no franchises/national chains; not a 2025 recipient.
programs.deadline: closed - 2026 cycle completed (announced Aug 24, 2026); next cycle TBD
programs.notes: 19 businesses received $10,000 in 2026. Annual cycle (a 2026 LinkedIn post said the cycle opened in March; not verified on an official page).
programs.source_quote: Guide: 'The 2026 Small Business Capitalization Program provides $10,000 grants to businesses that have been operating for three years or more' | Release (2026-08-24): 'MDEAT has completed its 2026 Business Empowerment Blueprint Grant Cycle'

programs.name: MDEAT Business Resource and Education Grant (start-up)
programs.administrator: Miami-Dade Economic Advocacy Trust (MDEAT)
programs.eligibility_detail: Miami-Dade businesses (and nonprofits) 6 months to 2 years old on Sunbiz; attend a workshop; never a previous recipient of this grant; no franchises.
programs.deadline: closed - 2026 cycle completed; next cycle TBD
programs.notes: 17 emerging businesses received $2,500 in 2026. One of the few grants for very young businesses.
programs.source_quote: Guide: 'the Business Resource and Education Grant offers $2,500 grants to businesses established for six months to two years' | Release: 'Business Resource Grant ($2,500): Awarded to 17 emerging businesses'

programs.name: Community-Based Organization (CBO) Grant Program for Human and Social Services
programs.administrator: Miami-Dade County Office of Management and Budget
programs.eligibility_detail: Nonprofit CBOs delivering human and social services in Miami-Dade.
programs.amount: $25,000-$600,000 per program per year (per the program description)
programs.deadline: closed - the CBO2425 grant process was canceled (Sept 2025); next cycle TBD
programs.notes: County allocates more than $15 million a year through CBO grants per the page, but the latest competitive process was canceled in the FY2025-26 budget. Good honesty example: don't send groups to it now.
programs.source_quote: 'Status of the Community-Based Organization (CBO) Grant Process for Human and Social Services (CBO2425): Canceled.' ... 'Grant size - $25,000-$600,000 per program per year.'

programs.name: Elevate Small Business Miami (Elevate Grant / Scale Up Miami)
programs.administrator: City of Miami, Office of the Mayor - Small Business Initiatives
programs.eligibility_detail: City of Miami small businesses. Elevate Grant (equipment, supplies, marketing, essential services) is listed as 'coming soon'; the Scale Up program's application date was April 20, 2026.
programs.deadline: closed - Scale Up applications were due April 20, 2026; Elevate Grant 'coming soon' (date TBD)
programs.notes: Site reports $3.2M+ in grants awarded historically. Contact: smallbusiness@miamigov.com (not contacted). Fetched via WebFetch (curl got 202 bot-check). Search snippet claims Scale Up pitch prizes up to $5,000 - not verified.
programs.source_quote: 'Program Dates - Apply by April 20, 2026' ... 'More Initiatives Coming Soon ... Elevate Grant: Receive a small business grant for equipment, supplies, marketing, and essential business services.'

unverified_left_out.name: Miami-Dade County Department of Cultural Affairs grants (Community Grants, Tourist Development Council, Artist Access, Summer Arts & Science Camps for Kids)
unverified_left_out.why: Search snippets show FY2026-27 deadlines (e.g. Community Grants Dec 3, 2026; TDC Jan 11, 2027; Artist Access Nov 23, 2026, max $2,000), but miamidadearts.org was down all morning on Oct 25, 2026 ('Temporary Service Interruption ... critical security updates'). Could not verify live, so left out. Likely the best OPEN Miami arts grants once the site is back: re-check before the pitch if possible.

unverified_left_out.name: Florida Job Growth Grant Fund (FloridaCommerce)
unverified_left_out.why: Verified live (https://www.floridajobs.org/jobgrowth) but left out: it funds public infrastructure and state-college/technical-center workforce training, and by statute 'may not be used for the exclusive benefit of any single company'. Not for small businesses or community groups.

unverified_left_out.why: Old floridajobs.org URLs now return 404; no current official page found this session. Left out.

unverified_left_out.why: Official URL from search (miamidade.gov/smallbusiness/bonding-financial-assistance-program.asp) returns 404. Left out.

unverified_left_out.why: PDFs exist on omnicra.com but are not linked from the current official program page, so their current status is unclear. Only the linked Microgrant is listed.

unverified_left_out.why: From press/aggregator snippets only, not on the official page. Amount left null.

unverified_left_out.why: Search says the deadline was extended to Aug 24, 2026 (now closed), but the official page content did not show dates. Left out.

unverified_left_out.why: Mentioned in search results (ITN 2026-01, up to $100,000 per award) but not verified on an official Children's Trust page this session.

unverified_left_out.name: Miami-Dade Beacon Council incentives (e.g. Targeted Jobs Incentive Fund)
unverified_left_out.why: Not verified this session; mostly aimed at relocating/expanding larger employers.

unverified_left_out.why: Listed as closed on dosgrants.com (6/1/2026 - 7/10/2026); amount not verified. Not listed separately.

unverified_left_out.why: Seen in search only (up to $10,000, business pays up to 15%); it is the CBO delivering the City facade program listed above, and its page was not fetched.
